title: Adic smooth base change
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its ring of integers $A=\mathcal O_E$, and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Consider a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
e\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
T&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Assume $f$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes noetherian [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\ell$ invertible on $S$. Use the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], indexed here by $n\geq0$ with $A_n=A/I^{n+1}$ and $I=(\varpi)$; every $A_n$ is finite of order invertible on the four schemes and perfect over $A$. At a corner $W$, the integral coefficient sheaf is $A_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$. Write $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)$ for its full subcategory of derived $I$-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Completed pullback is [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]; completed direct image means the restriction of ordinary $Ru_*$ to complete objects [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange].

Assume $T$ has finite dimension, as required for $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $K$ belong to that category, and suppose each canonical reduction
$$K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(A_n)_T$$
is in the essential image of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$ under the comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Then the canonical completed adjunction-mate exchange of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange]
$$
\alpha_K:Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp}}K
\longrightarrow Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp}}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K
$$
is an isomorphism in $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,A)$.

If $X$ also has finite dimension and there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every $n\geq0$, all four finite-coefficient objects
$$
Rg_{n,*}K_n,\qquad Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}K_n,\qquad Le_n^*K_n,\qquad Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*K_n
$$
have constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$, then both endpoints belong to $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $\alpha_K$ is an isomorphism in that full subcategory. The subscript $n$ on an operation denotes the same scheme morphism with coefficient sheaves $(A_n)_W$.

proof.text: The full-category definition [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] gives derived completeness of $K$. Put $P_m=A/I^m$ for $m\geq1$, so the datum's $P_m$ is this statement's $A_{m-1}$; no level is lost by the reindexing. Use the canonical reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], including its normalization maps. For each $n$, choose the assumed bounded constructible etale origin $L_n$ and an isomorphism $\nu_T^*L_n\simeq K_n$. By the finite-coefficient definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], this says $K_n\in\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$. These choices are used only to apply the finite theorem, not to define the integral map.

proof.text:
For each $n$ apply [sbc-thm-finite-proetale-smooth-base-change] with the finite ring $\Lambda=A_n$ and input $K_n$. Its finite-coefficient etale-origin condition is exactly the witness of step 1. If its phrase 'finite-level reductions' is read as further quotients by powers of $\varpi$, these are $A_n/(\varpi^r)=A_{\min(n,r-1)}$ for $r\geq1$, and the canonical normalization of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] identifies the corresponding reduction of $K_n$ with $K_{\min(n,r-1)}$. The witnesses in step 1 therefore cover these quotients as well. The square is cartesian, $f$ is smooth, $g$ is qcqs, and all schemes are noetherian. The order of $A_n$ annihilates its additive group and is invertible on $S$, so the finite theorem's underlying torsion smooth-base-change condition holds. Thus its canonical exchange
$$\delta_n:Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}K_n\longrightarrow Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*K_n$$
is invertible. This invokes no properness or preservation of constructibility by direct image.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change; finite pro-etale transport as in the cited node

proof.text: Write $G=Rg_*K$, $E=Le^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$, $B=Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp}}G$, and $D=Rh_*E$. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], $G$ and $D$ are complete once $K$ and $E$ are complete; by [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], $E$ and $B$ are complete and their reductions are the corresponding finite pullbacks of the actual reductions of their inputs. For the direct-image reductions use the canonical perfect projection maps of [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], first for $g$ and $K$, then for $h$ and $E$. These apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms because $P_m$ is perfect; the properness-only final clause is unused. Consequently the reductions of $G,E,B,D$, after restriction to their completed coefficient sheaves, are canonically isomorphic to the restrictions of $Rg_{n,*}K_n,Le_n^*K_n,Lf_n^*Rg_{n,*}K_n,Rh_{n,*}Le_n^*K_n$, respectively. To identify finite and integral operations after restriction, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_W=A_W$ and $S_W=(A_n)_W$ on each edge; the coefficient isomorphisms and their commutative projection squares are those of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. We claim these comparisons in the ambient completed-coefficient categories, and do not infer full faithfulness of derived restriction of scalars.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] for this square and complete $K$. It defines the specified map $\alpha_K$ by the completed unit, pullback-composition square, and counit, and identifies this very mate with the finite-level completed exchange under the canonical finite-reduction and direct-image/limit comparisons. In the notation of step 3, let $c_{B,n},c_{D,n}$ be the isomorphisms from the restrictions of the actual endpoint reductions to the restrictions of the finite endpoints. The identification gives the equation
$$c_{D,n}\,\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_K\otimes^L A_n)=\operatorname{Res}(\delta_n)\,c_{B,n}.$$
In particular every finite reduction of $\alpha_K$ becomes an isomorphism after restriction. Restriction reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], so these actual reductions are isomorphisms. The equality is provided by the cited mate comparison, not deduced from naturality alone or from faithfulness of derived evaluations.

proof.text: Both $B$ and $D$ are derived complete by step 3, and every canonical reduction of $\alpha_K:B\to D$ is invertible by steps 2 and 4. The final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-levelwise-isomorphism-cones] therefore proves that $\alpha_K$ itself is invertible. Both endpoints lie over $X$, since $f:X\to S$ and $h:Y\to X$. This proves the assertion in $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,A)$.

proof.text: Assume the extra interval condition. It applies in particular to the two finite endpoints in step 3. Their cohomology is therefore constructible and vanishes outside $[a,b]$. The isomorphisms of step 3 give $A_X$-linear isomorphisms on cohomology with the actual quotient-coefficient reductions $B_n,D_n$. These cohomology isomorphisms are $(A_n)_X$-linear: [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies $A_X/I^{n+1}A_X$ with $(A_n)_X$. Locally lift a section $r$ of $(A_n)_X$ to $\widetilde r$ in $A_X$. For such a cohomology isomorphism $\phi$, $\phi(rx)=\phi(\widetilde r x)=\widetilde r\phi(x)=r\phi(x)$. The identity is independent of the lift because $I^{n+1}$ kills both cohomology sheaves; local identities glue. Thus the actual $B_n,D_n$ are intrinsically constructible with the same interval. Their own canonical strict reduction towers and normalization cocycles are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity] separately to these two towers on the noetherian scheme $X$. It supplies common finite stratifications, pro-etale coverings, bounded adic-lisse finite-type local complexes and normalization-compatible reduction isomorphisms, precisely the full uniform-tower condition. No preservation theorem for a nonproper direct image is assumed.

proof.text:
We must also construct compatible etale-origin witnesses, which the full category definition requires. For either $J=B$ or $J=D$, choose $\gamma_n:\nu_X^*H_n\xrightarrow{\sim}J_n$ with $H_n$ bounded constructible, using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. For $m\geq n$ compute $H_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ on a K-flat resolution with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] the inverse image of that resolution is K-flat and inverse image commutes with the tensor. Exactness of comparison inverse image from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] computes it termwise. Thus
$$\nu_X^*(H_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)\simeq(\nu_X^*H_m)\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\simeq J_n.$$
The last isomorphism uses the normalization $\rho_{m,n}$ of the actual reduction tower [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. This etale tensor is bounded: its inverse image has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, exact inverse image commutes with cohomology, and the sheaf unit isomorphism of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] reflects zero cohomology sheaves. Hence [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] applies on $D^+$ with coefficient $A_n$. It uniquely lifts the isomorphism
$$\gamma_n^{-1}\rho_{m,n}(\gamma_m\otimes^L A_n)$$
to $\beta_{m,n}:H_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n$; lift its inverse as well. These satisfy $\gamma_n\nu_X^*\beta_{m,n}=\rho_{m,n}(\gamma_m\otimes^L A_n)$. For $k\geq m\geq n$, applying $\nu_X^*$ to the composite normalization and then composing with $\gamma_n$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma_n\nu_X^*\bigl(\beta_{m,n}(\beta_{k,m}\otimes^L A_n)\bigr)
&=\rho_{m,n}\bigl((\gamma_m\nu_X^*\beta_{k,m})\otimes^L A_n\bigr)\\
&=\rho_{m,n}(\rho_{k,m}\otimes^L A_n)(\gamma_k\otimes^L A_n)\\
&=\rho_{k,n}(\gamma_k\otimes^L A_n)
=\gamma_n\nu_X^*\beta_{k,n}.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel $\gamma_n$ and use faithfulness to obtain $\beta_{m,n}(\beta_{k,m}\otimes^L A_n)=\beta_{k,n}$. At equal indices the defining equation is $\gamma_n\nu_X^*\beta_{n,n}=\rho_{n,n}\gamma_n=\gamma_n$, since $\rho_{n,n}=1$. Cancellation and faithfulness give $\beta_{n,n}=1$. The tensor comparisons used here are the balanced tensor identifications on K-flat representatives, so their iterated reassociations have the same cocycle. This constructs the required compatible witnesses without borrowing a construction from the proof of another node.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, and bounded-below comparison; Tag 07A4, sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-tensor-product, and Tag 0G7E

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is noetherian of finite dimension in the conditional assertion, and $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ by pullback of its inverse on $S$. Completeness from step 3, uniform local models from step 6, and compatible witnesses from step 7 verify every membership clause of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] for $B,D$. This category is full: the map $\alpha_K$, its ambient inverse from step 5, and their two inverse identities are morphisms and identities in this same subcategory. The resulting isomorphism is therefore in $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

split_report.summary: Expanded the finite-reduction proof into eight steps, with general completed adjunction-mate comparison and derived-complete detection, and an explicit constructible-membership argument including normalization-compatible etale witnesses. Reused existing nodes only. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported landing was on S although both endpoints are on X; corrected to X and made the finite-dimension domain conditions of the existing Dbc notation explicit. Distinguished completed coefficient sheaves from finite constant coefficients. Removed the inapplicable proper-base-change theorem as a proof dependency.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the single blueprint proof paragraph: completed actions and perfect projection formula in steps 1 and 3; finite-level smooth exchange in step 2; identification of the specified completed mate in step 4; inverse-limit/completeness detection in step 5; constructible landing in steps 6-8. The unit sk-rem-rest is a roadmap with no numbered steps, and this node is not its key statement.

tool_uses.why: Provides completeness and direct-image/derived-limit commutation for arbitrary g and h; the smooth unit has no direct-image completion theorem.
Identifies actual reductions of completed pullback and supplies completeness for f and e; these are generic completion formulas, not a smooth-base-change assertion.
Identifies finite reductions of Rg_*K and Rh_*E using perfect quotient coefficients without properness; the unit supplies no projection formula.
Compares finite and completed coefficient operations after exact restriction and reflects isomorphisms; needed to type the reduction argument.
Supplies canonical inverse-image coefficient isomorphisms and commutative quotient squares needed for coefficient restriction along every edge.
Detects an isomorphism between complete objects from invertibility of all actual quotient reductions; no smoothness enters this general tool.
Provides A_X/I^m A_X = (A/I^m)_X to make cohomology comparisons quotient-linear; used only for coefficient bookkeeping in the conditional landing.
Turns a normalized reduction tower with constructible cohomology in one interval into the common local models required by the integral category; no base-change invertibility is asserted.
Provides bounded constructible etale origins of actual constructible endpoint reductions; this is a generic site-comparison equivalence.
Supplies tensor commutation and K-flat preservation under comparison inverse image to descend quotient normalizations of witnesses.
Supplies exact inverse image and its sheaf unit isomorphism, so the witness tensor is shown bounded before applying D+ full faithfulness.
Supplies bounded-below full faithfulness to lift normalizations and their inverses uniquely and prove the witness cocycle.
